title: Korean has 3 'necks'?! 🧣 #learnkorean
caption:
손목 (son-mok) = wrist = 손 hand + 목 neck 🧣
발목 (bal-mok) = ankle = 발 foot + 목 neck
So in Korean you have 3 "necks" — and Mongle has none 😂

Words in this video:
목 (mok) = neck
손목 (son-mok) = wrist
발목 (bal-mok) = ankle
으, 추워! (eu, chu-wo!) = brr, so cold!
목이… 셋?! (mo-gi… set?!) = three… necks?!
너도! (neo-do!) = you too!
내 목은…? (nae mo-geun…?) = where's my neck…?
따뜻해~ (tta-tteu-tae~) = so warm~

Tip: 목 is the narrow part that joins two bigger parts — your wrist joins hand and arm, your ankle joins foot and leg.

alt: A needle-felt miniature snowy street at dusk. A felt Korean boy shivers holding a mustard scarf next to Mongle, a coral felt blob mascot. A knitted banner reads In Korean, 3 body parts are 'necks'. He wraps the scarf around his neck: neck = 목 (mok). He pulls on mustard wrist warmers: wrist = 손목 (son-mok), 손 hand + 목 neck, while Mongle tilts and searches its own round side, thinking 손목…? (my wrist…?). He pulls long mustard socks over his ankles: ankle = 발목 (bal-mok), 발 foot + 목 neck. Seen from Mongle's low view, the boy spreads his arms with tags 목, 손목, 발목, and Mongle gasps 목이… 셋?! (three… necks?!). He kneels and puts a mint scarf on Mongle — 너도! (you too!) — but it slides down because Mongle has no neck: 내 목은…? (where's my neck…?). He winds the scarf round and round until Mongle is a cosy cocoon saying 따뜻해~ (so warm~), and a knitted banner recaps 손목 hand-neck = wrist, 발목 foot-neck = ankle.
